question: A 25-year-old baker is brought in by ambulance after a crush injury to his forearm. question: A 42-year-old man is brought to the emergency department via ambulance after he told his roommate he overdosed on moonshine in a suicide attempt 12 hours ago. question: Paramedics brought in a 50-year-old male with acute onset double vision and unsteady gait. question: A 5-year-old boy is brought in by his mother because he has had chest pain since he fell down their back steps and landed on his side earlier in the day. The patient points to the right posterior rib cage as the area where he has pain. This patient has never been evaluated in this hospital system before. Temperature is 37.2°C (99.0°F), pulse rate is 118/min, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 80/56 mmHg. Oxygen saturation is 99%. The patient appears nervous, is reluctant to talk, and avoids eye contact. The mother fidgets in her chair in the examination room. Physical examination shows linear bruises along the posterior ribs that appear to be in various stages of healing. The lungs are clear to auscultation, bilaterally. Abdominal examination shows mild tenderness to palpation in the right upper quadrant. X-ray studies of the chest and ribs show two posteromedial rib fractures along the right 7th and 8th ribs. When this finding is shared with the patient’s mother, she becomes anxious and wants to leave the clinic. In addition to treating the patient for his injury, which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
